requirements_summary: Privacore is building an enterprise RAG search for legal investigations. Primary needs: scalable embeddings index (50–200M docs projected), precise reranking to surface evidentiary passages, strict EU data residency and audit logging, SSO/SAML and KMS integration, retention controls and immutable audit trails. Operational constraints: prefer VPC/private control plane or on-prem option for final deployment. Cost sensitivity for high QPS: target $0.02-$0.05 per query (including embedding lookup + rerank).
latency_targets: Peak QPS 200, typical queries require p50 < 120ms (vector retrieval) and end-to-end p95 < 350ms after reranking for top-5 answers.
indexing_scale: Initial ingest target 50M docs (pdfs, emails, pleadings), long-term 150–200M. Average vector dim targeted 1536, expected index size ~20–40TB compressed depending on quantization.
cost_per_query_target: $0.02-$0.05 (including embeddings lookup + lightweight reranker); procurement wants modeled worst-case $0.08
reranking_strategy: Hybrid: ANN candidate retrieval (dense embeddings) followed by on-host lighter transformer reranker for passage scoring. Prefers ability to switch to a lower-cost distilled reranker under heavy load.
notes: Discovery notes: heavy emphasis on auditability — 'we need every analyst action logged to support FOIA and regulatory requests', CISO said.
AE note: Procurement timeline sensitive to security sign-off; legal team will review retention controls and deletion policies.
SE note: POC uses 5M doc sample; initial rerank p95 ~420ms with default reranker — goal to get below 350ms with quantized model and dedicated infra.
Customer quote: 'Accuracy on legal citations matters more than token-level fluff; reranker must preserve citation spans.'
Logistics: Wants EU-only VPC + option to migrate to customer-managed on-prem appliance for highest sensitivity cases.
Pricing ask: run two batch cost scenarios: (1) steady 20 QPS, (2) burst 250 QPS for short investigations — include caching impact from prefix/KV and query-level caching.
